value: Bihar — as undivided Bihar, the sense in which the question is answerable at all
reasoning: The question is defective on present boundaries: Mandar Hill stands in Banka district of Bihar, while Jhumri Telaiya lies in Koderma district of Jharkhand, so the two places are in different States and no single option is strictly correct. Both belonged to undivided Bihar before Jharkhand was carved out in 2000, which is the only reading under which the pairing makes sense and is almost certainly what the question intends.
basis: Both blind passes rated this LOW and BOTH independently identified the same defect and the same cause — the 2000 bifurcation of Bihar — splitting only on which least-bad label to attach, A choosing Bihar and B Jharkhand. Pass B even predicted A's answer in its own report and pre-emptively explained it as an artefact of the ambiguity rather than a real disagreement, which is exactly right: this is agreement on the finding, with a coin-flip on the label. Adjudicated to Bihar on an ASYMMETRY neither pass drew out. On present boundaries each option is half-correct — Bihar gets Mandar Hill, Jharkhand gets Jhumri Telaiya. But under the pre-2000 reading, which is the only reading in which BOTH places sit in one State and therefore the only one that makes the question well-formed, Bihar is correct for both and Jharkhand for neither. Bihar is therefore fully correct under one complete hypothesis and half-correct under the other, while Jharkhand is half-correct under one and wrong under the other; it is dominated. No official key exists for this paper. A student answering Jharkhand is not wrong on today's map, and the stored solution says so.
